summary: Sticky routing leak during canary cutover causes a subset of pinned sessions to be routed to canary instances
description:
Issue summary: During a weighted canary rollout for redwood-open-1.3.1-canary, a subset (~3%) of customer sessions that were previously pinned to redwood-open-1.3.0 started getting routed to canary instances despite the route pin.

Impact: NarrativeAI reports intermittent model mismatch for user sessions (incorrect responses, hallucinations) impacting production traffic (approx 3% of requests over the last 6 hours). Customers are seeing degraded quality for requests that should have remained on the pinned version.

Timeline: 2026-03-13 09:12 UTC - Canary rollout initiated (10% weight) via console. 2026-03-13 09:18 UTC - First customer complaint (NarrativeAI). 2026-03-13 09:30–15:00 UTC - Support and SRE triage, mitigations attempted. 2026-03-13 16:05 UTC - Canary weight rolled back to 0% as precaution. Issue persisted on a small fraction of sessions until 2026-03-13 18:40 UTC when a session-store eviction was triggered manually.

Steps to reproduce (internal): 1) Create a route with version pin to redwood-open-1.3.0 and active sessions. 2) Start a weighted canary rollout to redwood-open-1.3.1-canary (10% traffic). 3) Monitor session routing table and session-store keys during cutover and autoscaling events. 4) Observe that a small sample of pinned session IDs show route hash pointing at canary workers.

Observed behavior: - Pin metadata still present in route config. - Router logs show route decision mapping some pinned session tokens to canary pool. - Session-store shows duplicate entries for affected session IDs (stale session:canary and canonical:prod keys). - Affected requests return tokens and trace-ids that map to canary worker pods.

Hypothesis: A race between the canary-controller's assignment updates and the session-store eviction/replication window is causing transient duplicate session state. When an autoscaling event or pod drain happens in the serving pool, router fallback logic occasionally consults a slightly stale replica of session-store which contains a canary-assigned shard for the same session ID. This results in honor-ing the canary shard instead of the pinned route resolution.

Immediate mitigations applied: 1) Rolled back canary weight to 0% for the route. 2) Scoped a session-store eviction and consolidation job for NarrativeAI's route keys. 3) Temporarily increased router session-store read consistency to strict for the customer route.

Next steps: - Engineering to reproduce in staging with controlled autoscale/drain events. - Add stronger invariants to session-store write path to prevent dual-assignment during assignment reconciliation. - Add a diagnostic flag to console to surface session-store replica lag per route. - Postmortem to determine long-term fix and whether a small hotfix to router fallback ordering is warranted.
comments: [Support - Marisol Rivera 2026-03-13 09:42 UTC] Customer (NarrativeAI) reported that certain user sessions are returning an unexpected model variant; they confirmed they have a route pinned to redwood-open-1.3.0. Attached sample request ids: rq_8f3b, rq_8f4c.

[SRE - Liam Chen 2026-03-13 10:05 UTC] Initial triage: no global routing config change. Observed pod drain events in us-east serving pool at 09:20–09:27 UTC. Correlating router logs show ~2.8% of session tokens mapped to canary pool during that window. Increasing read quorum for session-store for affected route as temporary measure.

[Platform - Aisha Patel 2026-03-13 11:12 UTC] Hypothesis: race during assignment reconciliation + inconsistent session-store replicas. Spun up a replication consistency check job. Requested ability to force reconsolidation of route session keys via console (feature request logged).

[Support - Marisol Rivera 2026-03-13 16:20 UTC] We rolled canary back to 0% at customer's request. Customer still sees intermittent mismatches; they've asked for timeline on full mitigation and for a runbook describing how to validate pinned sessions after rollouts.

[SRE - Liam Chen 2026-03-13 18:45 UTC] Manual eviction/consolidation job completed for NarrativeAI keys. Observed affected session count drop to 0 after cleanup. Keeping ticket open for postmortem and code fix.
investigation_notes:
Key findings: 1) Router decision path prioritizes local session-store cache entries before authoritative route pin check if cache entry exists. 2) During rapid pool changes (drain + autoscale), session-store replicas can briefly contain assignments from in-flight canary reconciliation. 3) Affected requests correlated to specific serving pool drain windows. Reproduction in staging: created a route with 500 active sessions, triggered a concurrent canary roll and pod drain; observed ~1-4% leak under identical timing. Repro is intermittent and timing-sensitive.

Proposed fixes: A) Change router ordering to always validate route pin metadata as authoritative for pinned sessions before honoring session-store cached assignment. B) Add atomic compare-and-swap on session-store writes to prevent duplicate assignment keys. C) Improve session-store replication/consistency metrics surfaced in console. D) Add automated consolidation job as part of rollout lifecycle when weights change.
resolution: Mitigation: rolled canary to 0% and ran session-store consolidation which removed duplicate keys; increased read quorum for affected route. Long-term fix: engineering will implement router ordering change and CAS write for session-store (tracked in INT-3427). Customer update: NarrativeAI notified 2026-03-14 09:00 UTC with explanation, impact summary, and planned timeline for code fixes. Ticket will remain open until code changes are merged and validated in staging (target: 2026-04-01).
